description: Stereo enhancement by phase-shifted cross-cancellation - STEREO INPUT ONLY (mono refused 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: File ... is not of correct type (must be stereo)'). Empirically the algorithm is: subtract transfer x the opposite channel from each channel, then renormalize to the input's peak (a candidate model out_L = norm(L - t*R), out_R = norm(R - t*L) correlates 0.9997 with the render at t = 1 and t = 0.5; the binary logs 'Finding maximum input sample / Finding maximum output sample / Doing stereo enhancement'). The common (mid) content is cancelled in proportion to transfer, so the stereo image widens drastically: on a mostly-mono test file the side/mid RMS ratio went from 0.036 to 57.1 at the default transfer 1.0 (near-total mid removal, leaving anti-correlated side content) and to 0.108 at transfer 0.5. Duration static and sample-exact (1 s and 2 s stereo). transfer 0 is refused ('ERROR: Transfer parameter of ZERO produces no effect on the source.'). Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart).
musical_use: A width control with a violent top end. Low transfer (0.1-0.4) is the musical zone: partial mid cancellation pushes ambience, reverb tails and de-correlated detail outward while the centre survives - a wider, airier version of the same mix. The default 1.0 is effectively a MID KILL: what remains is the difference signal in anti-phase on both sides - enormous on headphones, but it collapses toward silence when summed to mono (the two channels cancel) - so treat high-transfer renders as an effect, not a mastering move, and always check the mono sum. Creative uses: extract a track's stereo ambience for reuse as a texture layer; exaggerate the movement of auto-panned or Haas-delayed material; make a near-mono source feel dispersed before granulation. On dual-mono (identical channels) input the default transfer nulls virtually everything - the renormalization then amplifies the residue, so expect noise-floor artifacts there.

transfer.description: Amount of the opposite channel used in the phase-cancellation (banner: '0-1: default 1 = all'). CDP-enforced 0 to 1 ('Parameter[1] Value (1.500000) out of range (0.000000 to 1.000000)'; -0.5 refused with the same quote) but 0 itself is refused at runtime ('Transfer parameter of ZERO produces no effect on the source.') - the curated minimum keeps it nonzero. 1.0 = near-total mid cancellation (side/mid RMS 57.1 on the probe file), 0.5 = moderate widening (0.108 from 0.036). Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.') - the width cannot vary over time; automate by cutting and processing sections.

examples.description: Gentle stereo widening that keeps the centre.
examples.expected_use: Same-length stereo output with ambience and side detail pushed outward; mono sum still substantially intact.

examples.description: Mid kill - keep only the stereo difference content.
examples.expected_use: Vocals/bass and anything centred largely vanish; what remains is anti-correlated width that cancels in a mono sum. Use as an effect or ambience-extraction layer.

known_issues: STEREO ONLY: mono input refused 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: File ... is not of correct type (must be stereo)' - the only mode-level channel constraint in this program (mode 1 accepts anything).

High transfer values produce ANTI-CORRELATED channels: the output sounds huge in headphones but sums toward silence in mono (the phase-cancellation trick is the point of the process). Check mono compatibility before committing.

The output is peak-renormalized to the input's level ('Finding maximum output sample' pass): on near-mono material the cancelled residue gets amplified back to full scale - quiet artifacts and noise floor become prominent. Dual-mono inputs are the degenerate case.
transfer 0 refused at runtime ('Transfer parameter of ZERO produces no effect on the source.') even though the quoted range includes it; the curated min is nonzero.
Duration static and sample-exact; deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart). transfer refuses breakpoint files (parameter 1).
